notes: Explosion during scheduled repair work between Kalinino and Yambakhtino, Vurnarsky District. Three gas service workers killed, one injured. Gazprom stated supply continued via parallel pipelines; no sustained throughput loss claimed. No attribution to hostile action.

Reactor unit shut down automatically after a turbine generator safety-system fault, reported by Rosenergoatom as a false alarm. Contributed to rolling outages across Krasnodar Krai and Rostov Oblast during a heatwave; DonEnergo attributed load stress partly to 39C+ temperatures. Capacity offline not quantified in open reporting.

Russia-Ukraine gas transit agreement of 30 December 2019 expired at 07:00 Kyiv time on 1 January 2025; transit via the Sudzha entry point ceased. Commercial and political termination rather than a sanction in the narrow sense - classified under the sanctions/supply-chain category because the taxonomy has no separate commercial-constraint class. Final pre-halt inflow recorded at 40.4 mcm on 31 December 2024.
Reported drone attack on the Kaleykino oil pumping station, a Druzhba transport hub in Tatarstan, attributed in reporting to Ukraine's SBU. Throughput effect not quantified in open sources.

Repeated drone strikes on the Unecha Druzhba pumping station in Bryansk Oblast during August 2025. Hungarian Foreign Minister Szijjarto confirmed Druzhba deliveries suspended. Day-level date not established across sources - recorded at month precision rather than inferred. Reports differ on the number of separate strikes in the month.

Crimea (internationally Ukrainian; tracked as a context unit, excluded from the Russia+Belarus ESDI). Ukrainian strike on 7 October 2024 on the JSC Marine Oil Terminal at Feodosia, the largest fuel storage facility in occupied Crimea. Satellite imagery reviewed by independent analysts showed 12 of 34 tanks hit, 8 completely destroyed. Multiple independent outlets plus satellite confirmation.

Electricity-sector event. Reported strike on the 750 kV Novobryanskaya substation in Bryansk Oblast; OSINT reporting cited ~500 MW of transmission throughput lost and a ~15% cut to electricity exports to Belarus. capacity_affected_mw here is transmission throughput, not generation removed, and is scored as an electric-power disruption with that caveat.

Electricity-sector event. Reported drone strike on the 110 kV Zheleznogorsk substation, Kursk Oblast, on 20 November 2025; ~16,000-20,000 customers reported without power. Customer-count effect only; no defensible generation-MW figure, so it is tracked and counted but not capacity-scored.

Electricity-sector event. Reported strike on the 110 kV Trubchevsk substation, Bryansk Oblast, ~October 2025; up to 15,000 residents reported without power, with hospital disruption and evacuations. Day-level date not firmly established across sources; recorded at month precision. Customer-count effect only, not capacity-scored.

Rosneft's Tuapse refinery struck in late January 2025, halting processing. Reuters (via industry sources) reported the primary crude unit CDU-12 repaired by late April and processing resumed around 6 May 2025 -- roughly three months. Recorded as a curated incident because the January 2025 strike is not enumerated at this date in the automated strike table; its observed reconstitution is carried in recovery.csv.
